scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Dances of Universal Peace were first formulated by Samuel L. Lewis, also known as Sufi Ahmed Murad Chisti.
The very first dance took place on 16 March 1968 in San Francisco, California.
The original dances were strongly influenced by Samuel Lewis's spiritual relationships with modern dance pioneer Ruth St. Denis and Sufi master Hazrat Inayat Khan.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The intention of the DUP is to raise consciousness and promote peace between diverse religions.
Dance leaders tend to believe peace can be promoted through experiencing the same One Joy through diverse dance steps, chants, and languages.
Dancing is seen as an opportunity to develop participants' spiritual awareness, hand-eye-body coordination, and competency in harmonizing with others.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Five to 500 dancers stand in a circle, often around a leader and musicians with acoustic instruments in the center.
All dances are participatory and spectating is somewhat discouraged because joy is the goal.
Dances are facilitated by a dance leader who often plays a drum, guitar, flute, or other stringed instrument.
Watch for Whirling.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The dances were originally performed at camps and meetings with a distinctly New Age and alternative feel.

Over time, they have increasingly been offered in diverse places of worship and more secular places such as schools, colleges, prisons, hospices, residential homes for those with special needs, and holistic health centers.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Samuel L. Lewis (Sufi Ahmed Murad Chisti) formulated the dances.
Ruth St. Denis and Hazrat Inayat Khan influenced Lewis's work.
The dances have developed into a global movement with members in 28 countries.

The tradition is of North American Sufic origin, drawing significant influence from Sufi practices such as Sema and The Whirling Dervishes, modern dance pioneers like Ruth St. Denis, and Rinzai Zen teachings.
